established_findings.statement: Large language models can translate high-level operator intent into candidate network configurations or configuration-relevant artifacts, and multiple prototype systems and benchmarks demonstrate feasibility.
limitations: Demonstrations are prototypical (papers/prototypes), not production deployments.
Reported accuracy/coverage depends on task subset, prompting/fine-tuning, and limited testbeds.

established_findings.statement: State-of-the-art LLMs produce useful draft network configurations but commonly exhibit egregious syntax, semantic, topology, and policy errors when used without deterministic verification.
limitations: Evaluation focused on specific use cases (router translation, policy implementation) and particular LLMs; error modes may vary by model and prompt.
Does not quantify every possible error class or all vendor CLIs.

established_findings.statement: Coupling LLM generation with deterministic network-verification tools (e.g., Batfish) or localized verifiers and using verifier-provided localized feedback substantially reduces errors and increases human automation leverage in configuration tasks.
established_findings.evidence_type: integration experiments and tool evolution reports
limitations: Reported gains (e.g., 6×–10× leverage) are task-specific and based on narrow case studies.
Scalability and multi-vendor generality are not fully demonstrated in these artifacts.

established_findings.statement: Iterative refinement/self-feedback and verifier-gate architectures (generate→verify→refine loops) are effective architectural patterns to improve correctness of LLM outputs in practice.
limitations: Effect sizes vary by task and verifier strength; some designs trade latency/cost for reliability.
Empirical evidence comes from dated/smaller-scale evaluations and simulated tasks.

established_findings.statement: Recent surveys and reviews identify safety, trustworthiness, verification-and-validation (V&V), provenance, and human oversight as central challenges when applying LLMs or agentic LLM systems to operational domains including networking.
limitations: Surveys summarize literature and open challenges but do not themselves provide new experimental evidence for specific NetOps interventions.
Operational prescriptions vary and often remain high-level.

established_findings.statement: Provenance-rich validation schemas, auditable logging, and verifier-triggered retry policies are proposed and shown useful to catch characteristic LLM extraction/generation errors in domain applications.
limitations: MAPLE-style validators were demonstrated in biomedical model calibration; direct NetOps-scale deployments and performance-cost tradeoffs require further study.
Audit architectures vary and require integration with enterprise change-control systems.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well LLM+verifier pipelines maintain correctness and safety at production scale across heterogeneous, multi-vendor real-world networks remains unresolved.
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: absence/limited-scope empirical evidence in supplied records
limitations: Existing studies demonstrate prototypes and case studies but do not provide broad production-scale evaluations across diverse vendor ecosystems.

unresolved_questions.statement: The robustness of LLM-driven NetOps pipelines to adversarial or correlated failure modes (malicious or accidental input perturbations that induce unsafe config changes) is not yet characterized in the supplied literature for NetOps-specific tasks.
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: general LLM robustness studies exist; NetOps-specific adversarial evaluations are absent in supplied records
limitations: Adversarial benchmarking work exists for LLMs in other domains, but direct NetOps adversarial evaluations are not present among the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: Operator trust, human–in–the–loop governance, and practical change-management integration strategies for LLM/agentic NetOps systems lack mature, empirically-validated models in the supplied set.
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: framework/proposal papers and surveys; limited empirical validation
limitations: Several proposals include human oversight in architecture, but operational studies measuring operator workload, failure-detection latency, and trust metrics in real NetOps teams are not present.

unresolved_questions.statement: The performance–cost tradeoffs (latency, verifier runtime, audit overhead) for closed-loop verify→refine NetOps pipelines across realistic change volumes remain incompletely quantified in the supplied literature.
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: architectural proposals and small-scale experiments; lacking system-level cost studies
limitations: Architectures describe metrics and tradeoffs; empirical end-to-end cost/latency studies at operator scale are not reported in the provided records.

candidate_gaps.statement: A standardized, operationally-oriented benchmark suite that measures functional correctness (reachability, policy compliance, connectivity), not just surface fluency, for LLM-generated network configurations is needed.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: benchmark/proposal papers and surveys indicating current evaluation limits
limitations: NetConfEval and related benchmarks exist but vary in scope; gap refers to broad community-standard operational correctness metrics and stress suites.

candidate_gaps.statement: Verifiers that produce actionable, localized correction feedback (not merely pass/fail) and automated repair APIs remain an area needing engineering and comparative evaluation for NetOps tasks.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: empirical study and tool evolution lessons
limitations: Verified Prompt Programming highlights need for localized feedback; large-scale comparative studies of verifier-feedback formats and automated repair workflows are lacking.

candidate_gaps.statement: Provenance, auditable change logs, and integration with enterprise change-control are underdeveloped for LLM-driven NetOps; reproducible validators and immutable audit trails need adaptation to NetOps workflows.
limitations: MAPLE and verifiable-audit proposals demonstrate principles in other domains; engineering and usability studies for network change-control integration are required.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical studies evaluating adversarial and correlated failure modes specific to NetOps (e.g., crafted intents that induce unsafe routing/firewall rules) are missing and would help quantify risk.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: indirect evidence from LLM robustness literature and NetOps failure analyses
limitations: Existing adversarial LLM assessments focus on bias/security in general tasks; NetOps-targeted adversarial frameworks are not documented in the supplied records.

excluded_claims: LLM-only systems (without deterministic verification) are production-ready and safe for autonomous network configuration deployment.
There is conclusive evidence in the supplied records that LLM-based NetOps systems scale to heterogeneous, multi-vendor production networks without additional engineering.
The supplied records prove that LLMs eliminate the need for human oversight in all NetOps change-management workflows.
